building_identity: Franklin Levering Cary Quadrangle (East), Purdue building code CQE, source FID 639

sources.geometry_method: Use returned WGS84 polygon; project each vertex with the repository-documented Purdue campus conversion; simplify collinear/noisy vertices with 0.12 m tolerance while retaining at least 9 vertices.
limitations: The source attributes Shape__Area and Shape__Length do not match area and perimeter measured from the returned polygon; the returned geometry is used for plan shape.
The source does not document units for Extrution=48. The builder interprets it as feet (14.63 m) only as a tentative overall height estimate.
GIS NUM_LEVELS and CountOfFLO both report 5, while the specific historical description reports 3 stories plus basement. The model shows three above-grade window levels and records this conflict.

sources.provider: Purdue Geospatial Data Science Lab / Indiana Digital Forestry
sources.product: Indiana 2017-2019 3DEP LiDAR Normalized Digital Height Model
sources.method: Sample raster values at cell centers inside the authoritative FID 639 footprint after transforming its WGS84 ring to EPSG:2968. All 474 interior cells are 36.67-61.07 ft above ground; median 46.20 ft (14.08 m), p10-p90 39.17-52.14 ft (11.94-15.89 m). Neighbor median in a 50-ft bounding box is 0.37 ft, while the neighbor p75 is 23.29 ft; this supports the building roof as the elevated surface, with edge/canopy caveats.
sources.use: Corroborates an approximate roof-surface height range and makes the 15.08 m modeled maximum plausible. It does not resolve floor-count convention, eave versus ridge heights, or exact roof form.
limitations: 5-ft cells can mix roof edges and vegetation; the automated GIS outline may include edge pixels.
NDHM reports normalized surface height, not a surveyed facade elevation or individual eave/ridge measurement.
The source's GIS Extrution=48 remains undocumented in units; its tentative feet interpretation is only corroborative.

sources.use: Purdue Archives dates this Cary Quadrangle exterior image to 1928. Visual inspection shows a long brick facade, three above-grade window rows, stone foundation band, repeated projecting gabled bays, and small attic windows. A separate building history identifies East as the first Cary unit and dates its opening to 1928, so this image may depict East; the catalog record does not identify the unit, so the match remains a chronology-based inference rather than verified identity.

model_interpretations: The official footprint is the strongest building-specific geometric source.

Three visible above-grade window rows follow the building-specific historic description. The historic source says three stories plus basement; two GIS fields say five levels. The count could include attic and basement in a different way, but the GIS field definitions do not establish that interpretation. The model shows three above-grade rows, an upper foundation band, and small attic windows only as an explicit period-context interpretation.

A Purdue Archives photo is dated to the same year Cary East opened, and it shows projecting gabled bays and small attic windows. It may depict East, but does not identify the unit; the match is a chronology-based inference. The gables, window rhythm, stone courses, pilasters, entrance placement, and pointed-arch treatment remain approximate interpretations rather than verified CQE details.

The 2018 NDHM samples corroborate an approximately 14.08 m median roof-surface height and 11.94-15.89 m p10-p90 range; the modeled 15.08 m maximum is plausible but remains an estimate, not a surveyed measurement. The GIS Extrution=48 field has undocumented units and is used only as tentative corroboration. NDHM cannot resolve eave/ridge height separately or settle the five-level versus three-stories-plus-basement conflict.
